4 · Ranked defects & suggested fixes (not applied)

1 · No night/dusk scenery lighting frames 61-72circuit data
Night frames are lit only by the car's headlamp pool; pole lamps (visible, unlit, at f83) and all stands stay dark; the snow-cap mountains stay light grey against a black sky. Cause: night:false (redbull.js:24) and lamp:"none" (redbull.js:60); the hand-built lamp poles (scenery/redbull.js:178-210) are plain boxes with a lamp colour and no emissive registration. Fix: either keep the circuit day-only and accept it, or register lamp heads through the lighting kit and add a night stand glow; check mountain snow colour vs night exposure in mountain() opts (:29-30). Mechanism is a guess from the source plus frames; the lighting registry was not read.
2 · Fog does not touch the sky frame 40 (f50 fog)engine
Terrain and far mountains haze but the sky stays full saturated blue and the horizon line is crisp. Likely the sky dome ignores fog density; look in js/lighting/atmosphere.js (guess; only fog frame f50 was examined closely). Not circuit-specific.
3 · Wet/rain turns pines into glassy ghosts frames 19-30, 43-48, 55-60, 67-72engine/renderer
Under wet/rain/storm the conifers render pale and translucent with noisy mirrored copies on the verge (stacked cone layers, hatch-like noise). Looks like a screen-space/planar reflection pass sampling vegetation; not tied to this circuit's code. Worth a renderer-debug pass.
4 · Storm ≈ rain frames 43-48 vs 25-30engine
Day storm is correctly dark grey (day-wet-lighting merge applied), but apart from streak density it is visually the same as rain; no lightning, wind or extra darkening. Compare js/race/weather-arc.js / atmosphere blend for a storm-specific term.
5 · Pale slatted stand reaches the verge at lap 0.83 frame 18circuit scenery, uncertain
A beige timber-looking block touches the green verge on the +1 side; stands at 0.80-0.88 use gap 8 m from the road edge (scenery/redbull.js:340-346: grandstandEx(0.80, 1, 8, 22, null, null, {livery:"crimson"…}), 0.88). The crimson livery did not show, and with the camera tilt the true clearance cannot be judged. Confirm with a plan-view probe; consider gap ≥ 12 m near a fast sweep.
6 · Docs and data disagree docs/tracks/redbull.md
Header says ~65 m elevation change (:3), §3 says ~53 m with grade capped at 5.5 % (:20-21). Measured 53.7 m range, 7.6 % peak (4 m sample) / 6.3 % (64 m). Also turn naming: scenery comments (:103-104) call 0.3036 "Turn 3 (Remus)" and 0.4913 "Turn 4", the def comment (redbull.js:46) calls 0.4913 "turns[2] Schlossgold"; the brief puts the T3 crest at ~0.22-0.30. Cosmetic, but a sourcing check against the real turn numbers is pending.
7 · 47 props silently dropped every build verify-track
tree=44, mountain=2, billboard=1 guard drops. Probably the forestEdge bands at distances 9-16 m colliding with the pit/guardrail zones, and mountains/billboards on the parallel stretch. Pre-filter like the existing backdrop() wrapper (:16-20) to remove the churn.
8 · Unsourced golden observation column source only
A 50 m gold column with red spire and "night-ready" light ring is placed at 0.30 (+1, 22 m), :373-387. It is not in the brief's landmark table and not in the landmark registry; no source cited. Not seen in a frame (not in any captured view). Either source it or remove it.
9 · Registry gap tests
redbull-wing and redbull-bull-plaza are required:true but tests/data/landmarks/redbull.json only registers the Lauda stand.
10 · Built length 0.7 % short measured vs claim
4288 m built vs 4307 (path.len) / ~4318 (real). Within tolerance; noted for the record.

5 · Code & scenery deep-dive

  • Frame ownership. The def sets no sceneryStartFrac; the comment (redbull.js:11-14) documents that a shift of 0.295 would put the paddock at Remus and plant 105 trees on the pit lane. Every anchor in the scenery file is therefore a direct racing fraction, correct as written.
  • Pit side. The pit complex and The Wing are on the +1 side (driver's right). Verified in the f00 frames: the orbit camera looks back at the car, so image-left is +1. The stand loop at 0.135 onward (+1) also sits on the right of the road.
  • Backdrop wrapper. backdrop() (:16-20) replicates the engine's onTrack cull to avoid ~295 guard drops per build; the remaining 47 come from other emitters.
  • Lamps. The lamp loops have per-side continue (not return) after a past bug that dropped half the poles (:185-189), skip the pit-owned side (pitSideLamp) and a verge zone 0.035-0.06.
  • Bank/terrain agreement. Zones are frac-keyed (redbull.js:45-52) with turn comments; they land within one run of each corner, consistent with bankingProfile re-seating.
  • Real-world cross-check. Brief cites redbullring.com (10 corners, T1 renamed for Niki Lauda 2019), formula1.com, oversteer48.com for stand names. Those URLs were not re-fetched this session; the stand set and bull statue are treated as claims. No stand sizes were measured against reality.
  • Style. All props are flat-shaded primitives; this file tags only the chairlift, chalets and camp props with MAT.* ids; whether the baked pack textures other props was not checked.

6 · Gallery · weather × time-of-day × lap position

Orbit camera is in front of the car looking back, so driver-right appears image-left. Images are downscaled and palette-quantised (192 colours) in the committed PNGs, which adds dither speckle on flat surfaces; this report embeds 800 px JPEG copies. Filenames: redbull-<nn>-f<lap%>-<view>-<tod>-<weather>.png (the f lap token is the sector slot of the gallery convention).

  • Coverage is 6 lap positions (0, .17, .33, .50, .67, .83), so the T1 apex (0.085), the Lauda stand (0.096), the stadium bowl (0.95), the bull plaza (0.10) and the golden column (0.30) were not framed on purpose.
